clue.text: Cook has minutes to find relish

indicators.note: to cook something up is to concoct it, so the letters of the following words are reworked

explanation.surface: A chef with a few minutes to spare tries to whip up some relish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' signals rearranging the ten letters of HAS MINUTES. 'Relish' looks like a condiment but means keen enjoyment.
explanation.definitionFit: Relish for a task is eager zest, the same keen pleasure as being fired up about it.

clue.text: Eat — and the rest start helping

parts.note: etc., short for et cetera, means 'and the rest'

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, here taken from 'helping'

explanation.surface: An invitation to eat, with everyone else getting their first helping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eat' is not about food: acid eats into metal, which is what etching does.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid etching corrodes a surface, just as rust is said to eat into iron.

clue.text: Volume rising in the average motorway

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters are read from bottom to top
the letters sit inside the words 'average motorway', straddling the gap

explanation.surface: A remark on the amount of traffic building up on a typical motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volume' suggests traffic, but it is a book. 'in' finds EMOT across 'averagE MOTorway'; 'rising' turns it upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A tome is a large, heavy book, and a volume is one book of a set or a book in general.

clue.text: Visit ruin — see different establishments

indicators.note: made different, the twelve letters of the three words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Tourist advice: tour a ruin and you will see some places unlike the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' signals rearranging VISIT RUIN SEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Universities are institutions of higher learning, and an establishment is any founded institution.

clue.text: Published — and is taken to court

parts.note: to be sued is to be taken to court in a lawsuit

explanation.surface: A book comes out and its author promptly faces a libel suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A publication is issued when it is put out to the public, as with stamps or a magazine.

clue.text: Polished cast covered debate

indicators.note: the word for cast wraps around the word for debate, covering it

parts.note: a snake casts or sheds its skin
to moot a point is to raise it for debate

explanation.surface: Actors refine a scene by smoothing over a dispute among the company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like actors; it is the verb meaning to throw off, as a snake sheds skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Something polished has had its rough edges rubbed even, the result of being made sleek.

clue.text: Worry about the Conservative left making a comeback

indicators.note: coming back means the group's name is read backwards

parts.note: in British politics 'the wets' were the moderate, left-leaning Tories opposed to Margaret Thatcher

explanation.surface: Fretting that moderate Tories might return to power.
explanation.walkthrough: WETS was Margaret Thatcher's name for the moderate wing of the British Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: To stew about a problem is to fret and brood over it anxiously.

clue.text: Rattling ensured mot failure

indicators.note: a failure here suggests things breaking down and falling apart, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written; the MOT is the annual British roadworthiness test for cars

explanation.surface: A driver is shaken that their car's annual test ended in failure.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is the UK's yearly vehicle safety test. 'failure' signals rearranging ENSURED MOT; 'Rattling' is not shaking but the informal 'rattling good'.
explanation.definitionFit: In old-fashioned British slang 'a rattling good yarn' is a splendid one, so rattling means great or terrific.

clue.text: Cinders with new dress — glass?

indicators.note: to dress something is to arrange it, so these letters are set out afresh

explanation.surface: Cinderella gets a new gown for the ball, so where's the glass slipper?
explanation.walkthrough: Cinders is Cinderella, whose glass slipper is the decoy. 'dress' signals rearranging CINDERS NEW; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's front window is a sheet of toughened glass, hence the question mark for an example.

clue.text: The delegates place an order

explanation.surface: A body of delegates makes a formal order.
explanation.definitionFit: A commission is a group appointed to act on others' behalf; to commission a work is to order it from an artist or maker.

clue.text: Check for noisy cats and dogs

indicators.note: something noisy is heard, so the word for heavy weather is taken by its sound

parts.note: it is raining cats and dogs means a downpour

explanation.surface: A check made to find which pets are making the racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cats and dogs' suggests pets, but stands for a downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in a horse or spending is to restrain it, as to check is to hold back.

clue.text: Established validity of protest by deputy head

parts.note: to demonstrate is to protest publicly, as on a march

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, here of 'deputy'

explanation.surface: A deputy head teacher stages a protest to prove a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deputy head' reads as a school role, but splits: 'head' takes the first letter of 'deputy'.
explanation.definitionFit: To demonstrate a claim is to prove it, showing by argument or example that it holds.

clue.text: She let nerves jangle all the same

indicators.note: jangled nerves are frayed and scrambled, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Despite her poise, a woman allowed her nerves to fray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jangle' signals rearranging SHE LET NERVES.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean however, used to concede a point and carry on regardless.

clue.text: Minute traces give grounds for doubt

explanation.surface: Tiny clues left behind cast doubt on a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspicion of garlic is a faint hint of it; suspicions are also mistrustful feelings that something is wrong.

clue.text: Being a friend, in a very private way

parts.note: a being is a creature or individual, a person
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Friendship conducted in a very private manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' looks like a verb but is a noun meaning a creature or individual.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something oneself, in one's own capacity and not through others, is a private, individual way of acting.

clue.text: Nations sea-change started engendering disquiet

parts.note: the UN is the United Nations

indicators.note: a change rearranges the letters of 'sea'
the word that started tells us to take only its opening letter

explanation.surface: A shift at sea among countries begins to cause anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sea-change' looks like one idea, but 'change' rearranges SEA into EAS; 'started' takes E from 'engendering'.
explanation.definitionFit: Unease and disquiet are both a feeling of anxious discomfort.

clue.text: Instrument of justice?

parts.note: reads as a tool of the law but means a musical pipe that shares its name with a part-time judge

explanation.definitionFit: It is a woodwind pipe, and in England also a barrister sitting as a part-time judge.

clue.text: Noted writer in company with mankind's first puzzle

indicators.note: the first of mankind is its opening letter

parts.note: a poser is a puzzling question

explanation.surface: A celebrated author joins a firm and asks the first riddle of humankind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' is a pun: a composer writes musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer writes music in notes, so is a writer of notes.

clue.text: Status one found in various options

indicators.note: the numeral is found within the rearranged letters
various means in assorted forms, so the letters of options are mixed up

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Social standing depends on having a number of choices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges OPTIONS into POSTION; 'found in' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: One's standing or rank in society or a ranking is one's place in it.

clue.text: Guarantee when positive

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
sure means certain or positive

explanation.surface: A promise given at the moment one feels certain.
explanation.definitionFit: To guarantee something is to promise it confidently, removing doubt.

clue.text: Coaches time run — and it never stops the leaders

parts.note: R is the cricket scoresheet abbreviation for a run

indicators.note: the leaders of the four words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Coaches running to a timetable that never stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coaches' looks like trainers or buses; it means rail carriages.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway carriages are called coaches, and a string of them makes up a locomotive's load.

clue.text: Modern-day argument against part-time

parts.note: a con is an argument against, as in pros and cons
temporary work is short-term, like part-time jobs

explanation.surface: A present-day case made against part-time working.
explanation.definitionFit: Contemporary means belonging to the present time, current.

clue.text: Soon to be incognito

explanation.surface: Someone about to go into hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old word for shortly; it is also short for anonymous, of someone unnamed.

clue.text: Fish rises, suddenly at first, from the sediment

indicators.note: in a down clue, rises means read upwards

parts.note: an eel is a fish

indicators.note: the word at first gives only its opening letter

explanation.surface: A fish suddenly surges up from the river bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' turns EEL upwards to LEE; 'at first' adds S from 'suddenly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lees are the dregs that settle at the bottom of a wine bottle or cask.

clue.text: Works executed with artist's materials

parts.note: paintings described by their medium; the same word names both the pictures and the paints used

explanation.definitionFit: Paintings done in oil paint are called by the paint's name, so the pictures and the medium share one word.

clue.text: One attitude adopted by fool needing aid

indicators.note: the stupid person comes first, taking on the following pieces after it

parts.note: an ass is a fool
the Roman numeral for one is I
a stance is an attitude or position

explanation.surface: A fool who takes up a fixed attitude needs help.
explanation.definitionFit: Assistance is help given, the same as aid.

clue.text: The way you start to cross the river

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a cross is the letter X

explanation.surface: Directions telling you how to begin crossing the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Styx is the river of the underworld in Greek myth, crossed by the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this is the underworld's main waterway, which Charon ferries the dead across.

clue.text: Rulers gifts accepted one day

indicators.note: the gifts accept the other letters, taking them inside

parts.note: presents are gifts
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Heads of state receive gifts on a single day.
explanation.definitionFit: Heads of state such as those of republics govern, so they are rulers.
